A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research on transformer weight spectra and small singular values. Their text, equations, figures and appendices support comparison. The substantial expansion and reorganization in v3 do not prevent matching retained material.

before.justification: v2 reports original spectral and activation analyses, Pythia perplexity interventions, BERT fine-tuning experiments on BoolQ, and CIFAR-10 experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 reports original transformer analyses, expanded pruning and fine-tuning experiments, GSM8K, RULER and HumanEval results, and numerical random-matrix simulations.

M1.justification: v3 introduces a proposed explanatory model absent from v2: a rank-one linear teacher, a two-layer student with fixed readout, a squared-error objective and a correlated-noise weight ensemble (Section 6). This substantially extends the modeling contribution; the existing transformer architectures and SVD/decile-zeroing procedure are retained.

E1.justification: v3 adds mathematical reasoning on GSM8K, code generation on HumanEval, long-context tasks on RULER, entailment on RTE and sentiment classification on SST2. WikiText, BookCorpus and BoolQ remain represented. The CIFAR-10 classification experiments from v2 Appendix A are removed.

E2.justification: v3 Appendix C adds a standard-coordinate-basis comparator to the activation-covariance-eigenbasis analysis, reporting its overlaps in Figure 13. The CIFAR-10 trained, lazy and frozen-layer comparisons disappear. Newly cited compression and quantization algorithms are discussed without new head-to-head evaluations.

E3.justification: v3 adds three-shot GSM8K evaluation, RULER testing with context length 8192, Llama perplexity interventions and single-layer decile removal (Appendix G). WikiText perplexity evaluations supplement the retained BookCorpus experiments. The stated MP reference-fitting prescription also changes from empirical matrix variance in v2 to cited noise-variance estimation in v3 Section 3.

E4.justification: New analyses examine basis specificity, layer sensitivity, outlier counts across model sizes and correspondence with particular activation directions (Appendices C and G–I). Figure 7 adds simulation-based validation of the theoretical model. The CIFAR-10 lazy/rich and frozen-layer pruning experiments are removed, while Pythia's temporal-overlap analysis is retained in Appendix A.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 7 reports five-seed error bars. v3 Figure 6 instead specifies three-sigma reference bands estimated from six unpruned runs, and adds random-matrix three-sigma overlap references and 100-draw ensemble averages. These change uncertainty reporting without establishing a uniform increase in replication of existing experiments.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include Llama GSM8K accuracy falling from the reported 43.2% baseline to 2.0% after removing the smallest Down-Projection decile (Table 1), and HumanEval accuracy falling from 32.32% to 0.0% under the corresponding intervention (Table 5). RULER, layerwise and additional fine-tuning results are also added; CIFAR-10 results are removed. These are additions and removals, not same-setting performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F add the teacher-student assumptions, correlated Gaussian weight ensemble, small-outlier formula, partition-function calculation and generalization-error derivation. These go substantially beyond v2's MP and lazy-learning mathematics. The new derivation contains errors, including Equation 23 differentiating Z where log Z is required.

C1.justification: v3 adds a central claim that a correlated-noise linear model explains informative small singular values, and positions the contribution more directly around SVD compression. It also qualifies v2's claim that small values become important only after fine-tuning: pruning before fine-tuning leaves measurable damage on RTE and SST2, although BoolQ can recover.

C2.justification: v3 adds a localization-based interpretation of the Llama matrices with weak covariance overlap, plus explicit limitations concerning functionally important directions missed by that overlap measure. It states that the proposed noise covariance requires validation across training runs and cautions against inferring scaling laws from three heterogeneous models. These are substantive qualifications beyond v2.

D1.justification: v3 adds V100 hardware information, estimates below 100 GPU hours for spectral/covariance calculations and below 1000 GPU hours for perplexity experiments, and numerical parameters for the new simulation. The code/data archive reference changes from record 14764226 to 15409885. These are documented resource and access changes; archive contents were not independently inspected.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion shifts substantially from task vectors, concept geometry and mechanistic interpretation toward activation-aware low-rank compression and quantization, including SVD-LLM, QuIP and SmoothQuant. New references on optimal low-rank approximation, random-matrix outlier transitions and statistical learning support the added theoretical positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Architecture notation and spectral background are merged, pruning and fine-tuning are combined, and training dynamics move to the appendix. Dedicated theory and limitations sections, a conference checklist and a reorganized appendix structure substantially change the narrative.

P2.justification: v3 changes to a single-column layout and extensively redesigns the displays. Spectral examples are organized by matrix shape, spectra and overlap panels are separated, and decile ordering is reversed. Five tables and new theoretical and diagnostic figures appear. Retained displays are also relocated, including v2 Figures 2 and 5 becoming v3 Figures 14 and 10.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's pruning evidence centered on Pythia and BoolQ, v3 tests the central claim across reasoning, coding, long-context tasks and additional fine-tuning tasks. New basis and layer controls probe important exceptions, while explicit limitations better qualify the conclusions. These substantially strengthen the paper's evidential support, outweighing the removed CIFAR-10 controls and localized derivation errors such as Appendix F, Equation 23. The explanatory model's noise assumptions still require validation in LLMs.
